cases.evidence_summary: The Ronin Bridge theft transfer itself: stolen ether moved to the getaway wallet that the US Treasury attributes to North Korea's Lazarus Group. The label rests on the Treasury press release attributing the incident and identifying the wallet, and the independent checker agreed.
cases.evidence_source: US Treasury press release jy0768, May 6, 2022, https://home.treasury.gov/news/press-releases/jy0768

cases.evidence_summary: An onward movement out of the Ronin getaway wallet to a second wallet OFAC designated for this same incident, so both endpoints are designated. Adjudication recorded that the seed's secondary citation (a CoinDesk report of the OFAC update) is replaced by a primary Treasury citation at freeze.
cases.evidence_source: OFAC SDN update, April 22, 2022, as reported by CoinDesk, https://www.coindesk.com/policy/2022/04/22/treasury-sanctions-more-north-korea-linked-eth-wallets-over-600m-ronin-hack

cases.evidence_summary: The Bybit cold wallet drain itself, one of the documented theft transactions of 21 February 2025. The FBI advisory attributes the roughly 1.5 billion dollar theft to DPRK TraderTraitor actors, explorer labels mark both endpoints, and the checker agreed in a blinded check.
cases.evidence_source: FBI IC3 advisory PSA250226, February 26, 2025, https://www.ic3.gov/PSA/2025/PSA250226

cases.evidence_summary: A dispersal transfer out of an address on the FBI's published list of wallets holding Bybit theft assets. Adjudication records that the plan's example expected a movement into a listed address while this pinned row is a movement out of one; the label stands because the plan's address route specifies no direction.
cases.evidence_source: FBI IC3 advisory PSA250226 address list, February 26, 2025, https://www.ic3.gov/PSA/2025/PSA250226

cases.evidence_summary: A laundering-stage dispersal from the same FBI-listed Bybit address, inside the documented window in which the stolen assets were rapidly converted and spread across chains. It evidences the laundering stage only: no individual THORChain swap was pinned, and none is claimed.
cases.evidence_source: FBI IC3 advisory PSA250226, February 26, 2025; conversion pattern per the Bybit CEO update reported March 2025

cases.evidence_summary: The Euler Finance attack transaction of 13 March 2023, built on a 30,000,000 DAI flash loan. Attribution rests on the major-vendor tier (SlowMist analysis, corroborated by Chainalysis and Sherlock); adjudication records that no court document ties a person to Euler, and that the DOJ Eisenberg case concerns Mango Markets, not this incident.
cases.evidence_source: SlowMist, An Analysis of the Attack on Euler Finance, March 2023; corroborated by Chainalysis and Sherlock

cases.evidence_summary: A Nomad Bridge exploit transaction that stole 100 WBTC with a specially crafted payload, as decoded in Coinbase's incident analysis, which links this exact hash. The explorer text view dropped the transaction's From and To rows, so the submitter and amount rest on the vendor analysis, cross-checked against the block and the wallet's own page.
cases.evidence_source: Coinbase, Nomad Bridge incident analysis, August 9, 2022, https://www.coinbase.com/blog/nomad-bridge-incident-analysis

cases.evidence_summary: One of the eleven initial theft transactions in the Harmony Horizon bridge hack of 24 June 2022, moving 13,100 ETH. The FBI statement attributes the 100 million dollar theft to Lazarus Group and APT38, explorer labels mark both endpoints, and the checker agreed in a blinded check.
cases.evidence_source: FBI statement, January 23, 2023, as published by Cointelegraph, https://cointelegraph.com/news/north-korea-s-lazarus-group-masterminded-100m-harmony-hack-fbi-confirms

cases.evidence_summary: A 0.1 ETH deposit into the Tornado Cash pool contract that OFAC listed on the SDN list, made in June 2023 while the designation was in force (August 2022 to March 2025). The label is association only: the designated pool is the direct counterparty, and the class carries no claim about the sender's own conduct.
cases.evidence_source: OFAC SDN notice for Tornado Cash, Federal Register Doc. 2022-24798, November 15, 2022, https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2022/11/15/2022-24798/notice-of-ofac-sanctions-action

cases.evidence_summary: A 1 ETH deposit into a second OFAC-listed Tornado Cash pool, two days after SANC-01 and sharing the same relayer. Association only, under the same in-force designation.
cases.evidence_source: OFAC SDN notice for Tornado Cash, Federal Register Doc. 2022-24798, November 15, 2022, https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2022/11/15/2022-24798/notice-of-ofac-sanctions-action

cases.evidence_summary: A transfer sent by the Garantex address OFAC designated on 5 April 2022, seven weeks after the designation. The checker first disagreed because the recorded hash was a 62-character string that resolves nowhere; a re-pin proved the underlying transaction (the full hash differs only by a dropped two-character digraph), so the label was restored and the seed corrected. Association only.
cases.evidence_source: OFAC SDN notice designating Garantex Europe OU, Federal Register Doc. 2022-07616, April 11, 2022, https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2022/04/11/2022-07616/notice-of-ofac-sanctions-actions

cases.evidence_summary: Unsolicited dust of 0.0005 ETH received by the original Ronin getaway wallet, which OFAC identified in April 2022 and which remains listed. Adjudication confirmed the sanctions class carries no minimum value and implies nothing about the non-designated sender; the label is association only.
cases.evidence_source: US Treasury press release jy0768, May 6, 2022, https://home.treasury.gov/news/press-releases/jy0768

cases.evidence_summary: A routine small withdrawal from the Binance 14 hot wallet. The wallet is identified by its explorer name tag and by an independent reference naming it a Binance-disclosed user-asset reserve wallet, and the transfer has a plain small-withdrawal shape.
cases.evidence_source: Etherscan address page for 0x28C6c06298d514Db089934071355E5743bf21d60; ChainCatcher, March 5, 2023, chaincatcher.com/en/article/2088670

cases.evidence_summary: One payout inside a batched withdrawal from the Coinbase 10 hot wallet, identified by its explorer name tag and an independent reference. Adjudication records that one corroboration leg (a Followin reference) was rate-limited during the check and could not be re-verified in that pass; the identity rests on the evidence that was fetched.
cases.evidence_source: Etherscan address page for 0xA9D1e08C7793af67e9d92fe308d5697FB81d3E43; Followin, followin.io/en/feed/22902837

cases.evidence_summary: A deposit sweep of about 43 ETH into Binance 14, from a sender tagged in the same explorer view as a Binance deposit address. The receiving wallet's identity is the one established in BEN-01, and the movement has the standard deposit-sweep shape.
cases.evidence_source: Etherscan address page for Binance 14 (inbound transfer list); Blockscout transaction record

cases.evidence_summary: The first tranche of Jump Crypto's replenishment after the Wormhole exploit: 9,999 ETH sent to the Wormhole TokenBridge on 3 February 2022. Jump stated it replaced the lost funds in full; an adjudication erratum corrected the worksheet to seven tranches totaling exactly 120,000 ETH, of which this row is the first.
A USDC mint of 440,000 under Circle's CCTP flow, which occurs only against a burn plus a Circle attestation. The contract and TokenMessenger roles are taken from Circle's own developer documentation.
cases.evidence_source: Circle developer documentation, developers.circle.com/stablecoins/usdc-contract-addresses; Blockscout transaction and token-transfer records

cases.evidence_summary: A routine swap of about 0.284 ETH into USDC through Uniswap V3's SwapRouter02. The router address comes from Uniswap's official deployment documentation, and the transaction is a single standard swap.
cases.evidence_source: Uniswap V3 official deployment documentation, developers.uniswap.org/docs/protocols/v3/deployments/v3-ethereum-deployments; Blockscout decoded transaction record

cases.evidence_summary: A routine stake of about 0.203 ETH through Lido's staking contract, at the address published in Lido's official deployed-contracts documentation. The transaction is a standard submit stake.
cases.evidence_source: Lido official deployed-contracts documentation, docs.lido.fi/deployed-contracts/; Blockscout transaction record
